scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 1, grouped verses 11.1.6–11.1.7.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवम् अवतार-प्रयोजनं सर्वं सम्पाद्य स्वं लोकं जगामेत्य् आह श्लोक-द्वयेन---स्व-मूर्त्येति । लोकानां लावण्यस्य निर्मुक्तिस् त्यागो यया । याम् अपेक्ष्य लोकेषु लावण्यं नास्तीत्य् अर्थाह् । यद् व, लोकेभ्यो लावण्यस्य निर्मुक्तिर् दानं यतः । यत्-सम्पर्केण लोका लावण्यवन्तो भवन्तीत्य् अर्थः । तया स्व-मूर्त्या नृणां लोचनम् आच्छिद्य आकृष्य ततोऽन्यस्यावलोकने लोचनस्याप्रवृत्तेः । तथा स्व-गीर्भिस् ता गिरः स्मरतां चित्तं च आच्छिद्य । तथा पदैस् तत्र तत्राङ्कितैस् तानि पदानि ईक्षताम् ईक्षमाणानाम् अन्यतो गमनादिकाः क्रियाश् चाच्छिद्य । तदानीन्तनानां सर्वेषां चक्षुर्-आदि-प्रवृत्तीः स्वैक-निष्ठाः कृत्वेत्य् अर्थः । किं च, इत उपरि जनिष्यमाणानां संसार-तरणाय कौ पृथिव्यां शोभनाः श्लोकाः सुश्लोकाः कवीनां यस्यां तां स्व-कीर्तिं वितत्य विस्तार्य, अनया कीर्त्या अञ्जसा सुखेनैव नु निश्चितं तमस् तरिष्यन्तीत्य् अभिप्रेत्य ईश्वरः स्वं पदं स्थानम् अगाद् इति ॥६-७॥
word_for_word: having accomplished the entire purpose of the descent
that he went to his own realm
the beauty of the worlds or people
there is no beauty in the worlds
by that very form of his
because the eyes no longer act
and the minds of those who remember
of all those living at that time
the activities of the eyes and other faculties
having made them devoted to himself alone
of those to be born afterward
entries.literal_english: Having fulfilled every purpose of his descent, the Lord went to his own world: this is stated in the two verses beginning ‘by his own form.’ One interpretation of his form is that it casts aside the beauty of the worlds, for there is no beauty in the world by comparison with it. Alternatively, it bestows beauty on the worlds, since people become beautiful through contact with it. With that form he captured human eyes, which ceased to look upon anything else; by his words he similarly seized the words and minds of those who remembered them; by the footprints marked here and there he drew away the acts of those who beheld them, including going elsewhere. In this way all the activities of the eyes and other faculties of those then living became fixed upon him alone. Further, for the sake of those to be born later crossing worldly existence, he spread his own fame on earth in fine verses composed by poets, thinking: ‘Through this fame they will certainly cross darkness with ease.’ Thus the Lord went to his own abode.
entries.note: One Śrīdhara source block is marked 11.1.6–7. The two alternative explanations of beauty as surpassed and beauty as bestowed are both recorded. Other commentators' expansions are excluded.
